name: Firmware Update

claims.claim_text: The standard mechanism is a bootloader: a small program resident in flash that runs first at power-up, checks the application image for validity and transfers execution to it if the image is good.
claims.quote_verbatim: You'll have a little bootloader, which is a small program that resides in Flash. And when the device boots up, it runs this bootloader first.
claims.speaker: Trey German
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Trey German - Launchpad Laden Lodesman

claims.claim_text: Updating requires a path for the application to re-enter the bootloader, after which the new application is received over whatever communication channel is available; any interface capable of getting data into the chip will serve, including CAN, USB and a plain UART.
claims.quote_verbatim: Really, any way that you can get information into a chip, you can use to load applications into it.
claims.speaker: Trey German
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Trey German - Launchpad Laden Lodesman

claims.claim_text: The reason such a mechanism exists in vehicles is that the modules are not physically accessible: a microcontroller distributed through a car cannot be removed, opened and reprogrammed through its debug header when a defect is found.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can't really pull those things out of the car and open them up, plug into the JTAG header, and reprogram them.
claims.speaker: Trey German
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Trey German - Launchpad Laden Lodesman

claims.claim_text: The same mechanism is an attack surface: access to the vehicle's internal bus, for example through an attached wireless device, makes it possible to reprogram parts of the car.
claims.quote_verbatim: Would it be possible for someone to try and reprogram parts of a car kind of thing? Absolutely.
claims.speaker: Trey German
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Trey German - Launchpad Laden Lodesman

claims.claim_text: In a car, one module downloads the update and distributes it over the internal bus to whichever module is listening, across what are typically several buses.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's like basically something that's downloading all the firmware updates and then pushing them over the can
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Every microcontroller in a modern connected vehicle can be updated over the air and routinely is, which forces per-module version tracking across the whole vehicle.
claims.quote_verbatim: Every little mic controller in that car can get, get updated over the air and they very routinely are.
claims.speaker: Joris Aerts
claims.episode_title: Satellites and EVs with Joris Aerts

claims.claim_text: The financial contrast between recall and remote update is stark: one vulnerability required recalling roughly two and a half million vehicles, while another manufacturer pushed an over-the-air fix to every affected car before the vulnerability was even disclosed publicly.
claims.quote_verbatim: pushed out an over-the-air firmware update to fix vulnerability in every single car. So they didn't have to do a recall.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: A Security Update with Michael Ossmann

claims.claim_text: That capability is itself the way in, since the over-the-air path is a route for an attacker as well as for the manufacturer.
claims.quote_verbatim: that is a potential way in for hackers, that over-the-air thing
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: A Security Update with Michael Ossmann

claims.claim_text: Vehicle internal networks are effectively open, or partitioned into a few weakly isolated open networks, so control of one device on the bus generally extends to control of many.
claims.quote_verbatim: it doesn't take much to go from a foothold or control of one device on that CAN bus to gaining access or control over many devices on that CAN bus
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: A Security Update with Michael Ossmann

claims.claim_text: Remote updates must be staged rather than broadcast: a proportion of a tenth of a percent of the fleet is seeded first, then one percent, then ten, because a bad image cannot be recalled once it has gone to everyone.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to give like 0.1% of the units, you know, start seeding the new firmware image
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: An interview with Alvaro and Jen from the URE Podcast

claims.claim_text: Updating a thousand devices and updating a million are different problems, and the difference is what makes staged rollout necessary rather than optional.
claims.quote_verbatim: Firmware update for 1,000 devices is different from a million devices.
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: An interview with Alvaro and Jen from the URE Podcast

claims.claim_text: Building the over-the-air update capability first is a development strategy rather than a shipping feature: it lets alpha units be distributed to testers who then receive every subsequent build, replacing a cycle in which each unit was physically posted back to be reflashed.
claims.quote_verbatim: the first thing I do when I start on a project is I make sure I have the capability of OTAing my device
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: An interview with Alvaro and Jen from the URE Podcast

claims.claim_text: The image programmed at the factory is flashed three to four months before the product reaches a customer, so what must be guaranteed is that it boots, reaches the backend and updates itself to the current release on day zero.
claims.quote_verbatim: my gold master, which gets flashed into a product three to four months ahead of when we actually have the product land in someone's hands
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: An interview with Alvaro and Jen from the URE Podcast

claims.claim_text: The cost of easy updating is discipline: when a defect can be fixed by sending another update, the incentive to test thoroughly before release erodes, and the burden shifts to the customer who must keep updating.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you can just send another update and fix it, why spend all this time testing it to make sure it works in the first place?
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: An interview with Alvaro and Jen from the URE Podcast

claims.claim_text: The security requirement on a remote update path is that nobody else can perform the update on the manufacturer's behalf.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't want someone else to do the firmware update for you
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto
claims.episode_title: An interview with Alvaro and Jen from the URE Podcast

claims.claim_text: The ability to push an update later produces a materially different engineering mindset from custom silicon, where a spin can cost millions of dollars and there is no field fix.
claims.quote_verbatim: the ASIC designers have a different viewpoint. Cause they know there's so much on the line
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Products increasingly ship unfinished on the assumption that the update will complete them, which is why an out-of-the-box update is often required before a device does anything useful.
claims.quote_verbatim: one of the reasons that you have to often have to update the firmware right out of the box is because the product isn't finished when they manufacture it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Treating that as normal is argued to be the harmful direction, since it licenses shipping poor products on the reasoning that firmware will fix them later.
claims.quote_verbatim: Oh, we can fix it later in firmware. I think it's a dangerous direction.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A device requiring an update every couple of days indicates that testing was skipped, and there is a hard boundary on what firmware can repair: a wrong resistor value is not fixable in software.
claims.quote_verbatim: sometimes it's like a firmware update and the resistor value is wrong
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: The update mechanism is itself the thing most likely to break and the hardest to recover: without regression testing, a change that made the image slightly larger altered the image layout, broke the device firmware update path and bricked units in the field.
claims.quote_verbatim: we'd break like, you know, DFU and like, you know, we'd, the image would be slightly bigger
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: Where the product is sealed, losing the update path is terminal rather than inconvenient: recovering the device means drilling into it, and for an encased consumer product the unit is simply written off.
claims.quote_verbatim: that then basic effectively bricks it until you then go and drill into it or open it back up
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: In the absence of automated regression testing, the compensating practice was extensive manual exercise of the device before every push, with the update mechanism the item watched most closely.
claims.quote_verbatim: but DFU was the biggest one that we worried about
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: Even a change unrelated to a feature can break it: an adjustment to a message parser stopped notifications arriving although the modified code path was not the one involved.
claims.quote_verbatim: the change we made didn't even like affect that part of it, but we broke it
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: The update system can be where the vulnerability lives: one defect was found in the read-only memory routine provided to handle updates, raising the question of what to do when the updating mechanism itself is broken.
claims.quote_verbatim: The vulnerability was in the ROM itself to be able to handle an update.
claims.speaker: Laura Abbott
claims.episode_title: Finding Hardware Flaws with Laura Abbott

claims.claim_text: The mitigation adopted was to abandon the vendor's update path entirely and write their own bootloader, which meant taking on flash partitioning for robust image updates and the versioning scheme along with it.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're going to be on our own to be able to write update code
claims.speaker: Laura Abbott
claims.episode_title: Finding Hardware Flaws with Laura Abbott

claims.claim_text: Rollback policy is a design decision with no clean answer: permitting a return to an older image reintroduces that version's defects, while allowing only forward movement fixes some defects and may introduce others.
claims.quote_verbatim: only a rel, allow rollbacks to an older version, or that might also have a different set of bugs
claims.speaker: Laura Abbott
claims.episode_title: Finding Hardware Flaws with Laura Abbott

claims.claim_text: Automated validation of a new image can only confirm the tests that were written for it, so an image can pass every check and still be broken in a way nothing looked for; this is the standing nightmare scenario for automatic updating.
claims.quote_verbatim: It only knows how to pass the tests that you've put in front of it.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Finding Hardware Flaws with Laura Abbott

claims.claim_text: Server firmware is updated far less often than would be desirable, and in practice the major updates appear only after a catastrophic defect.
claims.quote_verbatim: it only seems to come out when there's, you know, some sort of catastrophic bug
claims.speaker: Laura Abbott
claims.episode_title: Finding Hardware Flaws with Laura Abbott

claims.claim_text: Firmware is now recognised as part of the software supply chain and as a vector in its own right, so every part of a system has to be considered for what could be done maliciously through it.
claims.quote_verbatim: firmware itself can be vulnerable to
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Finding Hardware Flaws with Laura Abbott

claims.claim_text: Where the whole software stack is certified, as in medical devices, firmware updates cannot be shipped without recertification, which makes that update cycle unviable for security maintenance.
claims.quote_verbatim: they even can't roll firmware updates without getting recertified
claims.speaker: Dmitry Nedospasov
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching with Michael Ossmann and Dmitry Nedospazov

claims.claim_text: The recommended structure is a certified bootloader that can be locked down and uses sound cryptography to prevent malicious images being accepted, followed by regular tested updates on a schedule.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need to have a certified USB bootloader that you can lock down and use some sort of decent cryptography
claims.speaker: Dmitry Nedospasov
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching with Michael Ossmann and Dmitry Nedospazov

claims.claim_text: Device firmware upgrade, usually abbreviated DFU, is a standard USB mechanism for uploading a new image, entered by holding a button at power-up and intended to make replacement possible with minimal risk of needing a hardware debug adapter to recover.
claims.quote_verbatim: DFU is, uh, device firmware upgrade
claims.speaker: Sylvain Minot

claims.claim_text: Pairing that low-level mechanism with a mass-storage presentation, so the device appears as a small USB drive for ordinary files, covers both the risky update path and everyday file transfer with standardised protocols.
claims.quote_verbatim: So you have DFU for the low-level stuff that you want to update. And for the rest, there's a file system.
claims.speaker: Jeroen Domburg

claims.claim_text: The same standardised approach lets a programmable-logic bitstream and the soft processor application running alongside it both be replaced in the field.
claims.quote_verbatim: what allow people to replace the FPGA bitstream
claims.speaker: Sylvain Minot

claims.claim_text: A wireless update flow on a small microcontroller works by having the running application listen for an upgrade command, receive the compiled image wirelessly, store it in an external flash chip, and reboot.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can send it a command saying, okay, I need you to upgrade the firmware
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: On the next boot the bootloader detects the new image in the external flash, erases the old application, writes the new one and jumps to it.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's going to see there's a new flash image or new program to be flashed on the Atmega
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A similar arrangement was built by expanding the bootloader region of a part chosen for having more space, deriving the bootloader from an existing open-source one, and adding an external SPI flash the bootloader can also boot from, with the application downloading an Intel hex file into that flash.
claims.quote_verbatim: I made it so that that bootloader can also boot from the spy flash
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vic Aprea - Federated Firmware Functionalism

claims.claim_text: Verifying the image before committing it protects against a corrupted transfer but not against a valid image that is wrong: a bad file published with a matching checksum still passes, and that residual risk is accepted rather than solved.
claims.quote_verbatim: I could still screw it up by putting a bad hex file on the server with a bad check file to go with it
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vic Aprea - Federated Firmware Functionalism

claims.claim_text: Booting the whole firmware from a removable card removes the bricking risk entirely, because a bad image can be replaced by swapping the card.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's no brick in your SD card. No, you can't brick this one.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: With a card-based update path every firmware defect is recoverable in the field, with the single exception of a defect inside the bootloader itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: Any firmware issue I can fix with the soft, with the SD card update. Huh. Except. So the only real risk is if it's hardware. Except inside the bootloader.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A card-based path was chosen over wireless updating on one instrument because implementing the wireless route was assessed as a great deal of work, and updates are infrequent enough that removing a battery cover to reach the card is acceptable.
claims.quote_verbatim: we can do it, but it's a crap ton of work
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Loading an update from a card also avoids requiring the user to have a serial interface, which is how most instruments that support updating at all do it.
claims.quote_verbatim: Most of them are like through the serial port
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The contrary judgement is that wireless updating is worth the effort even where a card slot exists, because sending someone firmware becomes a matter of opening an application and uploading it rather than shipping media.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can, like, ship off firmware to someone and it's literally like, hey, open this app, upload it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The cost of that capability is memory: a bootloader chain and the space to hold a second image consume substantially more of the device's storage.
claims.quote_verbatim: it it just takes up a lot more memory
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An over-the-air update on a Bluetooth part is arranged with a bootloader alongside the vendor's radio stack, so that a phone application can load a new image and the enclosure never has to be opened.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can use the NRF Connect app and load a new piece of firmware in there
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Memory budget determines whether a product can be updated at all: halving the available flash may remove the space needed to hold a second image, which eliminates the update capability and with it a product function.
claims.quote_verbatim: that might actually prevent you from not being able to store an additional firmware image in there for like a firmware upgrade
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: That constraint argues for fitting the larger memory part from the outset, because a shipped unit cannot be changed and early customers would otherwise be excluded from firmware that needs more space than their device has.
claims.quote_verbatim: once you ship them, you can't update them
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Cost reduction and update capability pull against each other, and the sequence that works is to get the product working and shipped before attempting to cost down.
claims.quote_verbatim: this is not the time to cost down
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The update feature is a common casualty of a processor that turns out to be too small: on one programme, at the third physical prototype, the manufacturer reported that everything would not fit and proposed dropping firmware updating.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're going to have to leave out this, you know, the firmware update feature
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A working device with a broken update path is routinely presented as complete, with the missing capability described as a detail.
claims.quote_verbatim: You know, firmware update doesn't work, but that's just a feature. That's just details.
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: A design invariant worth engineering towards is that no update can leave the device in a state where it cannot be connected to and reprogrammed, which takes deliberate work to guarantee.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're never able to get it in a state where you can't connect to it and reprogram it
claims.speaker: Colin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: A poorly designed update procedure bricks devices outright, leaving the unit stuck at power-up with no recovery path short of an external programmer.
claims.quote_verbatim: the firmware update procedure is retarded in it, and I bricked it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Firmware, Netburner and Semiconductors - Chris's Capitalism Colloquy

claims.claim_text: A defective update pushed to a fleet of home devices bricked a large number of them at once, which is the fleet-scale form of the same failure.
claims.quote_verbatim: they had a firmware update that bricked a bunch of this stuff too
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An embedded Linux image built with a distribution builder was given a power-on self test and an automatic fall-back to the previous image, so that an update interrupted by loss of power does not brick the device.
claims.quote_verbatim: did a nice power on self test and fail back to the previous image
claims.speaker: Ariel Briner

claims.claim_text: Firmware updates are not performed over satellite links because the cost in both power and data is prohibitive, and are done over cellular where coverage allows.
claims.quote_verbatim: we don't do firmware updates over satellite just because of, of, of costs, both in power and data
claims.speaker: Alvaro Prieto

claims.claim_text: Updating firmware on a spacecraft is a high-risk operation, which is part of the appeal of running an interpreted language on a stable core: functionality is changed by uploading a file for the interpreter to run rather than by reflashing the firmware itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: when they update the firmware, it's a very scary nail-biting process
claims.speaker: Tony DiCola

claims.claim_text: The number of processors in a product is limited in practice by the difficulty of delivering firmware updates to all of them.
claims.quote_verbatim: The biggest con I've come up with is delivery of like firmware updates.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Wearables Might Have Limited Fashion Options - Lachrymogenic Lane Language

claims.claim_text: Self-programming parts allow a large deployed population to be updated at once: two thousand microcontrollers in an installation were reprogrammed in about two seconds.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can also upgrade all the firmware in one, literally two seconds, you can update the firmware in 2,000 pics
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: How the device will be programmed — at the factory, by a technician, over the air from a cloud service, or over the air from a phone — has to be decided early, because the firmware architecture, the security model for getting an image onto the device and the backend that serves it all follow from that choice.
claims.quote_verbatim: Is it going to be programmed at the factory? Is it going to be programmed by a technician? Is it going to be programmed over the air?
claims.speaker: Jonathan Beri
claims.episode_title: Why IoT Is Difficult with Jonathan Beri

claims.claim_text: Deferring that decision is what makes it unrecoverable: omitting something as small as the button that puts the device into update mode cannot be corrected once the hardware exists.
claims.quote_verbatim: You don't remember to put in the DFU button or something simple like that
claims.speaker: Jonathan Beri
claims.episode_title: Why IoT Is Difficult with Jonathan Beri

claims.claim_text: Production programming and field updating are separate stages: a bootstrap image loaded at the factory runs a power-on self test that a production operator can act on without further knowledge, after which the device connects to a server and pulls the current firmware.
claims.quote_verbatim: someone at the production facility without having any other knowledge they can like say yes this is working
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Like a steam engine in your house

claims.claim_text: Fleet management platforms show which of the deployed units are active and which firmware revision each carries, and manage the migration between revisions as well as delivering the images.
claims.quote_verbatim: eighty of them have this. Certain firmware revision. And then you can. You can manage migrations
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Doing that in house requires two distinct competencies: hooks in the firmware capable of replacing the running image, and a cloud component to serve and track it, the latter being a separate discipline from embedded work.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need to have some kind of hooks in the firmware, right?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Fleet software is not only about the image: it also has to report status and confirm devices are alive while they sleep, and carry small amounts of data.
claims.quote_verbatim: most of these also need status and verifying things are awake occasionally while still sleeping
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A platform vendor's operating system absorbs that overhead, handling the transfer, checksum verification and swap so a developer changes code and clicks a button, which is a substantial amount of firmware work to have done for you.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a lot of firmware overhead to do these kind of things
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The dependency is visible when the vendor stops: customers whose devices ran on such a platform keep working but stop receiving updates, and must take over development themselves.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could go and develop it yourself, but it's just they're not going to push the updates anymore
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A hosted update service also solves distributed development: a collaborator elsewhere presses reset, the device calls home and fetches the version the other engineer uploaded, without needing the full development environment locally.
claims.quote_verbatim: he just has to press the reset button and then it calls home and gets a new version
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A device incapable of being updated is a permanent vulnerability, and at fleet scale the practical obstacle is not the mechanism but locating the units at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: even if you wanted to. You couldn't probably go and find all of them. And get them all updated.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The converse also holds: the ability to update a device remotely is itself a vulnerability, so both the presence and the absence of the capability carry security cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: The ability to remote update something. That's also a vulnerability.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Whether a connected device continues to receive updates, rather than its power consumption, is what determines its useful life.
claims.quote_verbatim: Is it getting firmware updates?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The difficulty of upgrading connected consumer products is what makes any vulnerability in them durable.
claims.quote_verbatim: the problem is upgrading, right? It's really hard to upgrade these.
claims.speaker: Samy Kamkar

claims.claim_text: Intercepting an update in transit gives an attacker a trusted device inside an otherwise private network, from which further attacks can be launched.
claims.quote_verbatim: say you hijack the firmware update when that's coming down to whatever this device is
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Design Reviews Are Important - Habitual Hype Hebetude

claims.claim_text: Peripherals and cables now carry updatable microcontrollers: a USB-C to VGA adapter was found to expose direct firmware update, allowing its firmware to be read out and replaced, and any cable doing more than basic USB contains a microcontroller.
claims.quote_verbatim: direct firmware update is available on this USB microcontroller. I can dump the firmware off of this device.
claims.speaker: Joe Fitzpatrick

claims.claim_text: Forcing a device into firmware update mode is a recognised attack step, used to move sensitive memory contents into a readable state; in one device the critical values were copied into RAM at power-up on the assumption that the chip's security would prevent RAM being read.
claims.quote_verbatim: you glitch the device and then you basically have the firmware of the treasure go into this firmware update mode
claims.episode_title: New Life Skills with Joe Grand

claims.claim_text: Understanding a vendor's firmware update file format is what makes third-party firmware possible, and documentation of that format for one product line was extended to a related one.
claims.quote_verbatim: able to understand a little bit about the Canon's firmware update files
claims.speaker: Trammell Hudson

claims.claim_text: Most hardware never receives a firmware update after sale, because the manufacturer's involvement ends when the unit ships.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of this hardware never, ever sees any firmware updates
claims.speaker: Trammell Hudson

claims.claim_text: Open firmware changes that calculus in three ways: vulnerabilities are found and patched by a far larger community than the few dozen people at a firmware vendor, owners can patch on their own schedule, and a community can continue supporting hardware its manufacturer has abandoned.
claims.quote_verbatim: this lets us take advantage of the fact that everyone is looking for security vulnerabilities in Linux
claims.speaker: Trammell Hudson

claims.claim_text: The same option exists at consumer scale: an off-the-shelf device can be opened and reflashed with community firmware that its owner can then update as often as they choose, where the vendor's own product may never be updated.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can spin your own firmware updates and you can update them as, as, as much or as little as you want
claims.speaker: Keith Burzinski
claims.episode_title: Automating the Home with Keith Burzinski

claims.claim_text: Whether a purchased device is genuinely owned is put in question by mandatory updates that can change its permitted behaviour, such as revising the geographic restrictions on where an aircraft may be flown.
claims.quote_verbatim: do they force you to get like the firmware updates, which then change the geo

claims.claim_text: Firmware updates are used to unlock capability the hardware already had: a spectrum analyser's resolution bandwidth improved from ten hertz to one hertz through an update alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: the new firmware update turns it into one Hertz

claims.claim_text: The same pattern appears as a paid upgrade: a video product's higher model differed from the cheaper one by a firmware upgrade costing several hundred dollars, roughly a third of the product price, with the hardware likely identical.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was literally just a firmware upgrade
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An update can also add an entirely new function to a shipped product, such as a handheld recorder gaining the ability to operate as a USB microphone.
claims.quote_verbatim: this now acts as a USB mic
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In infrastructure the return can be measured directly: updating the firmware of data-centre power supplies to switch more efficiently converts a fraction of a percent of efficiency into significant money across thousands of machines.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can go in and update the firmware of the device and, you know, see real financial gain from that
claims.speaker: Trey German
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Trey German - Launchpad Laden Lodesman

claims.claim_text: Putting a processor into a previously analogue product buys the ability to push fixes: control-loop constants that once required sending an engineer to solder resistors are changed through a menu, and a software mitigation can hold a customer's process running until a hardware fix is exchanged.
claims.quote_verbatim: You had to send a guy out to solder some resistors. Oh, wow. Now they can do it through the menus.
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: A telecommunications standard was deployed faster than its competitor because operators needed only to update the firmware of existing infrastructure, whereas the alternative required capital investment in new equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: all they had to do is update their existing infrastructure with some firmware updates
claims.speaker: Jared Wolff

claims.claim_text: Reconfigurable logic placed in servers for future use can be reprogrammed remotely to add hardware acceleration, with speed-ups reported from ten to a thousand times; the corresponding risk is that a faulty configuration pushed to a hundred thousand machines takes them all down.
claims.quote_verbatim: they can just remotely update the configuration of these FPGAs
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Longevity is designed for by dividing the product: the parts physically fixed in place are specified to last, while the parts that must stay current are made field-serviceable so they can be swapped rather than updated indefinitely.
claims.quote_verbatim: the product has been physically designed in such a way that some of it is easy to field service and swap out
claims.speaker: Kerry Scharfglass

claims.claim_text: Instruments whose readings carry safety consequences restrict updating: one meter's firmware can be updated only by dealers holding the programmer, on the reasoning that a reprogrammed meter reporting zero on a live circuit could kill its user.
claims.quote_verbatim: Only the dealers can do it just in case there's a new firmware release and you've got stock
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Most instruments in that class historically used one-time-programmable parts, so the unit bought was the unit kept, and moving to a flash-based microcontroller was what made bug-fix updates possible at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: most multimeters on the market have a one-time programmable chip in there
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Where updating exists but is not exposed to users, it is performed at the factory through an internal header or a bed-of-nails fixture, with the consequence that two units of the same model bought at different times probably carry different firmware.
claims.quote_verbatim: I guarantee that the meter that you bought, the meter that you bought last year has, and if you buy the same meter again, now it probably has different firmware in it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: European regulation now requires that a device carrying the conformity mark and having a programming port be updatable, with a stated commitment to supply updates and respond to disclosed critical vulnerabilities; devices using one-time-programmable memory fall outside it.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it does have a programming port, it has to be updatable
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The objection to mandating updatability is that adding a programming path adds an attack vector, so the requirement trades one class of risk for another.
claims.quote_verbatim: making it programmable makes it an attack. You're adding an attack vector
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Writing the update code against the published protocol rather than the specific vendor's part means the controller can in principle be substituted with any compliant device years later without changing the code.
claims.quote_verbatim: we could just switch it out with any other power delivery controller chip and our code should still just work
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A controller chip already in the design for another purpose can carry the update path: remote debugging of the main processor and firmware updating were both routed over an isolated serial interface through the USB power-delivery controller.
claims.quote_verbatim: we can do remote debugging of our main microcontroller over the isolated serial interface
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Presenting the device as a standard human-interface and storage class gives driverless updating, so a user drops the file onto the device rather than installing tooling.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're also using HID and storage HID for driverless use
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Delivering an update through a web browser over a serial connection, using the bootloader's own transport protocol, removes the need for a separate command-line tool or vendor desktop application.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can do firmware updates through the browser
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A capability delivered as a firmware update rather than a hardware change is far easier for a customer to adopt, because nothing about their existing hardware has to change and the software can simply be removed if it does not work out.
claims.quote_verbatim: here's a bit of firmware, do a software update and you can start testing it tomorrow
claims.speaker: Alex Haro
claims.episode_title: Space Age Bluetooth with Alex Haro

claims.claim_text: A module vendor that publishes each new firmware release at no additional cost and makes upgrading straightforward removes the risk of being dependent on the manufacturer or having to buy a new part to get a fix.
claims.quote_verbatim: they give you the latest firmware whenever they publish it. And there's no added cost in there.
claims.speaker: Jeff Roberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Rowberg - Mini Module Master

claims.claim_text: A firmware update can reveal the true cause of a hardware problem: a battery failure attributed publicly to mechanical design was mitigated by an update limiting charging to sixty percent of capacity, which is not a plausible remedy for a mechanical fault.
claims.quote_verbatim: samsung pushed out a firmware update that limits charging to 60 of the battery
claims.speaker: Stephen Craig

claims.claim_text: A recurring self-inflicted debugging failure is spending a day chasing a defect while repeatedly loading the old image and never actually applying the update.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've spent the whole day downloading the old code image and you never actually updated it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
